featured_reviews.name: Pooja K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Citylight Cinema for a Sunday evening show recently. Overall, the theatre experience was actually not bad. For around ₹400, we got two tickets for a weekend evening show, which felt quite reasonable. The theatre was also pretty packed, so clearly a lot of people visit this place regularly.

The main disappointment was the food section. They had a large variety of items displayed on the menu screens, but most of them were not available. Only popcorn, samosas, nachos, and a paneer tikka sandwich were being served. Nothing else from the menu seemed available.

If you’re displaying so many food options, especially during a busy weekend evening show when people are likely to snack more, the counters should be better stocked. It creates unnecessary disappointment when customers see multiple items advertised but can’t actually order them.

Overall: decent theatre experience and fair ticket pricing, but the food availability definitely needs improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Sarthak Choudhary
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently watched *Dhurandhar 2* at Chitra Cinema, and it turned out to be a surprisingly enjoyable experience.

I opted for the lounger seats, and they were quite comfortable, making the whole movie-watching experience much more relaxed. The seating arrangement gives you enough space to sit back and enjoy the film without feeling cramped, which is a big plus.

One of the best parts about this theatre is the affordability. Unlike most places today, the food and snacks here are reasonably priced, so you can actually enjoy your popcorn and drinks without feeling like you overspent. It adds to the overall value for money.

The vibe of the theatre has that classic single-screen charm, but with decent maintenance and a good viewing experience. If you’re looking for a budget-friendly movie outing with comfortable seating in Mumbai, Chitra Cinema in Dadar East is definitely worth considering.

​The biggest letdown was the audio quality. In this era of advanced surround sound and Dolby systems, this theater feels like it is stuck in the past. The sound was flat, muffled, and lacked any depth. Honestly, it felt like listening to a movie on a cheap Bluetooth speaker rather than a professional cinema hall system. The bass was nonexistent, and the dialogue was barely clear.the screen quality was poor. A theater is supposed to provide an immersive experience, but this place failed on every front. I highly recommend avoiding this theater until they completely upgrade their sound system and facilities. It is a total waste of time and money.

Overview
Cinépolis is one of the most popular multiplex chains in Mumbai, known for its sleek, modern design and high-end cinematic technology. Whether you are visiting the one in Andheri, Thane, or Navi Mumbai, the vibe is consistently premium. It’s a top-tier choice for movie-goers who prioritize comfort, crystal-clear visuals, and a great atmosphere for a day out with friends or family.
Pros:
Superior Comfort: The seating is well-spaced with excellent legroom. If you opt for the VIP or IMAX screens, the leather recliners are incredibly cozy.
Cutting-Edge Tech: They use advanced laser projection and Dolby Atmos sound systems, making the action feel very immersive.
Variety of Formats: Depending on the location, you can choose from 4DX (moving seats/effects), IMAX, or their luxury "Coffee Tree" service.
Cleanliness: The lobbies and washrooms are generally well-maintained and have a "high-class" feel.
Cons:
Expensive Concessions: Like most premium malls, the popcorn and sodas are quite pricey—sometimes costing more than the movie ticket itself!
Peak Hour Crowds: During big blockbuster releases or weekends, the lobby can get very crowded, leading to long queues at the security check and food counters.
Parking Fees: Since most Cinépolis theaters are inside major malls, you’ll have to pay the standard (and sometimes steep) mall parking rates.

Movie Max Goregaon - Honest Review

Visited Movie Max Goregaon with friends to watch Pushpa 2, but the experience was disappointing for several reasons:

1. Parking Charges: The two-wheeler parking fee is ₹50, which is very high for a single-screen theater. Even premium theaters like PVR or INOX charge less.

2. Toilet Facilities: The number of toilets was very limited, leading to long queues. The toilets were also very small, which was inconvenient for the crowd.

3. Drinking Water: There was no drinking water facility available, which was surprising and inconvenient for the audience.

4. Sound Quality: The sound system was not loud enough, and I missed many dialogues during the movie. This was a major letdown.

Overall, the theater didn’t meet basic expectations for comfort or amenities. I might not visit again unless these issues are addressed. Would recommend exploring better theaters in the area for a more enjoyable movie experience.

description:
FilmFool is a film club and movie screening space in Mumbai dedicated to supporting filmmakers and film enthusiasts. Along with curating our own Film screenings and cinema conversations, we also provide our venue to filmmakers who wish to present their work.

Our space includes:
•⁠ ⁠A 150 inch with 100% cinema DCI-P3 gamut coverage.
•⁠ ⁠A 7.1 Dolby sound system.
•⁠ ⁠An intimate and comfortable environment designed for focused viewing.

If you are looking for a venue for your movie screenings in Mumbai, we would be happy to connect and give you a walkthrough. If not, we are also open to discussing possible collaborations or partnerships that can further strengthen the film community.

owner_posts.post_text:
This February, Filmfool invites you to experience love through cinema — not as a single idea, but in all its forms, contradictions, and quiet moments. 🎞️❤️

We’re hosting Feature February, a month of intimate screenings featuring three beautiful films that revolve around love, relationships, memory, and connection — each followed by space for conversation and reflection.

✨ 14th February — Before Sunrise
A Valentine’s Day screening of a film that understands romance through conversations, chance meetings, and the feeling of time standing still.

✨ 21st February — Badhaai Do
Followed by a special discussion with Akshat Ghildiyal, writer of Badhaai Do, exploring the anatomy of commercial love story writing in Bollywood.

✨ 28th February — Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
A deeply moving film about memory, heartbreak, and the desire to hold on — or let go.

Each screening is intentionally intimate, created for audiences who enjoy watching films together and staying back to talk about them.

featured_reviews.name: Parikshit Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited MovieTime Cinemas at Hub Mall with a group of friends on a Friday, expecting a good movie experience, but it turned out to be quite disappointing.

The experience started on a positive note. The security staff were welcoming, the common area was clean, and there were plenty of food options available. However, the popcorn wasn’t worth the price.

The washrooms were also decently maintained. The real disappointment began when we entered the auditorium. There was a strong foul smell throughout the hall, making it very uncomfortable to sit. The seats were old, broken, and clearly not maintained for a long time. What surprised us even more was that the auditorium wasn’t cleaned after the previous show empty popcorn tubs, Coke cups, and other litter were still lying around. There were even mosquitoes and flies inside the hall, which completely ruined the overall experience.

The only reason I’m not giving a one-star rating is because the screen quality and sound system were actually quite good.

For a theatre in a mall, basic hygiene and maintenance should never be compromised. I sincerely hope the management focuses on cleaning the auditoriums and renovating the seating, as the current condition is far below expectations.

Cleanliness: 1/5
Seat Comfort: 1/5
Screen Quality: 3/5
Sound Quality: 3/5
Food & Beverages: 2/5
Staff: 4/5
Value for Money: 2/5

Overall Rating: ⭐⭐

Good screen and sound can’t make up for poor hygiene, broken seats, and an unpleasant auditorium. A complete maintenance upgrade is urgently needed.
